# Chapter 1: Introduction to computers

<!-- BEGIN HEADER (generated by tools/build.py) -->
> [Home](../../../../README.md) › [Part I — Computer Science Foundations](../../index.md) › [1. Computer Fundamentals](../index.md) › Chapter 1: Introduction to computers

- **Status:** Drafted · 8 syllabus topics
<!-- END HEADER -->

This chapter builds the mental model that every later chapter relies on. It starts with the definition of a computer and the cycle every computer follows (input, processing, output and storage), separates hardware from software, surveys the kinds of computers you will meet from microcontrollers to supercomputers, and ends with the client and server roles and the difference between computing locally and remotely.

By the end you should be able to look at any device, from a thermostat to a data centre, and say what its inputs, processing, outputs and storage are, where its software runs, and which machine is doing the work.

Read the lessons in order; the first is the foundation for the other two.
